spots.name: Vasa Museum
spots.summary: The Vasa Museum is a maritime museum in Stockholm, Sweden. Located on the island of Djurgården, the museum displays the only almost fully intact 17th-century ship that has ever been salvaged, the 64-gun warship Vasa that sank on her maiden voyage in 1628. The Vasa Museum opened in 1990.

spots.name: Stockholm Palace
spots.summary: Stockholm Palace, or the Royal Palace, is the official residence and major royal palace of the Swedish monarch. Stockholm Palace is in Stadsholmen, in Gamla stan in the capital, Stockholm. It neighbours the Riksdag building.

spots.name: Storkyrkan
spots.summary: Storkyrkan, also called Stockholms domkyrka and Sankt Nikolai kyrka, is the oldest church in Stockholm. Storkyrkan lies in the centre of Stockholm in Gamla stan, between Stockholm Palace and Stortorget, the old main square of Stockholm.

spots.name: Sager House
spots.summary: The Sager House or Sager Palace is the official residence of the prime minister of Sweden, located at Strömgatan 18 in central Stockholm.

photo.author: Sagerska huset 2012 - h.jpg: I99pema derivative work: ArildV

spots.name: Skansen
spots.summary: Skansen is the oldest open-air museum and zoo in Sweden located on the island Djurgården in Stockholm, Sweden. It was opened on 11 October 1891 by Artur Hazelius (1833–1901) to show the way of life in the different parts of Sweden before the industrial era.

spots.name: Tre Kronor

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Tre Kronor or Three Crowns Castle was a castle located in Stockholm, Sweden, on the site where Stockholm Palace is today. It is believed to have been a citadel that Birger Jarl built into a royal castle in the middle of the 13th century.

spots.name: Stockholm Central Station
spots.summary: Stockholm Central Station or Stockholm C is the main railway station in Stockholm, and largest railway station in Sweden in terms of passenger numbers and train traffic. It is located in the Norrmalm district of central Stockholm on Vasagatan, extending from Vattugatan in the south to Kungsbron in the north.

spots.name: Skogskyrkogården
spots.summary: Skogskyrkogården is a cemetery located in the Gamla Enskede district south of central Stockholm, Sweden. It was inaugurated in 1920 and was inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List in 1994.

spots.name: KTH Royal Institute of Technology
spots.summary: KTH Royal Institute of Technology, abbreviated KTH, is a public research university in Stockholm, Sweden. KTH conducts research and education in engineering and technology and is Sweden's largest technical university. Since 2018, KTH consists of five schools with four campuses in and around Stockholm.

spots.name: Nationalmuseum

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: Nationalmuseum is the national gallery of fine arts of Sweden, located on the peninsula Blasieholmen in central Stockholm.

spots.name: Rosenbad
spots.summary: Rosenbad is a building in central Stockholm, precinct of Norrmalm. It is a building owned by the Swedish state and serves as the seat of the Government. The present government of Sweden is the right-leaning Kristersson Cabinet.

spots.name: Gustav Adolfs torg
spots.summary: Gustav Adolfs torg is a public square in central Stockholm, Sweden.

spots.name: Nordic Museum
spots.summary: The Nordic Museum is a museum located on Djurgården, an island in central Stockholm, Sweden, dedicated to the cultural history and ethnography of Sweden from the early modern period to the contemporary period.

spots.name: Stortorget
spots.summary: Stortorget is a public square in Gamla Stan, the old town in central Stockholm, Sweden. It is the oldest square in Stockholm, the historical centre on which the medieval urban conglomeration gradually came into being.

spots.name: Riddarholmen Church
spots.summary: Riddarholmen Church is the church of the former medieval Greyfriars Monastery in Stockholm, Sweden. The church serves as the final resting place of most Swedish monarchs.

spots.name: Sergels torg
spots.summary: Sergels torg is a major public square in Stockholm, Sweden, constructed in the 1960s and named after 18th-century sculptor Johan Tobias Sergel, whose workshop was once located north of the square.

photo.author: Original photographer: Anders Bengtsson; Image merging / retouching: Waldir

spots.name: Nobel Prize Museum
spots.summary: The Nobel Prize Museum is located in the former Stock Exchange Building on the north side of the square Stortorget in Gamla Stan, the old town in central Stockholm, Sweden.

spots.name: Arvfurstens palats

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Arvfurstens palats is a palace located at Gustav Adolfs Torg in central Stockholm. Originally a private residence, it has been the seat of the Swedish Ministry of Foreign Affairs since 1906.

spots.name: Livrustkammaren

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: The Royal Armoury is a museum in the Royal Palace in Stockholm, Sweden. It contains many artifacts of Swedish military history and Swedish royalty.

spots.name: Saint George and the Dragon
spots.summary: Saint George and the Dragon is a late medieval wooden sculpture depicting the legend of Saint George and the Dragon, located in Storkyrkan in Stockholm, Sweden. It is attributed to Bernt Notke and was commissioned by the Swedish regent Sten Sture the Elder. It was inaugurated in 1489.

spots.name: Gröna Lund
spots.summary: Gröna Lund, or colloquially Grönan, is an amusement park in Stockholm, Sweden. Located on the seaward side of Djurgården, it is 3.8 ha in size, relatively small compared to other amusement parks, mainly because of its central location, which limits expansion.

spots.name: Drottninggatan
spots.summary: Drottninggatan in Stockholm, Sweden, is a major pedestrian street. It stretches north from the bridge Riksbron at Norrström, in the district of Norrmalm, to Observatorielunden in the district of Vasastaden.

photo.author: No machine-readable author provided. Svante björkum assumed (based on copyright

spots.name: Katarina Elevator
spots.summary: The Katarina Elevator or Katarina Lift is a passenger elevator in Stockholm that connects Slussen to the heights of Södermalm. The lift was a shortcut between Katarinavägen, Slussen and Mosebacke torg.

spots.name: German Church
spots.summary: The German Church, sometimes called St. Gertrude's Church, is a church in Gamla stan, the old town in central Stockholm, Sweden, belonging to the German Saint Gertrude Parish of the Church of Sweden.

spots.name: Kungsträdgården
spots.summary: Kungsträdgården is a park in central Stockholm, Sweden. It is colloquially known as Kungsan.

spots.name: Järnpojke
spots.summary: Järnpojke or Iron Boy is a sculpture in Gamla stan of Stockholm, Sweden by Liss Eriksson, which is only 15 centimetres (5.9 in) high and therefore is the smallest public monument of Stockholm.

spots.name: Hallwyl Museum

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: Hallwyl Museum is a Swedish national museum housed in the historical Hallwyl House in central Stockholm located on 4, Hamngatan facing Berzelii Park. The house once belonged to the Count and Countess von Hallwyl, but was donated to the Swedish state in 1920 to eventually become a museum.

spots.name: Klara Church
spots.summary: The Church of Saint Clare or Klara Church is a church in central Stockholm. A church has been at the site since the 1280s; the current buildings date from the sixteenth through nineteenth centuries. Since 1989, the Swedish Evangelical Mission is responsible for its activities.

spots.name: Hötorget
spots.summary: Hötorget (Haymarket) is a city square in the center of Stockholm, Sweden that has been transitioning since the Early Medieval Period.

spots.name: Hedvig Eleonora Church

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Hedvig Eleonora Church is a church in central Stockholm, Sweden. It is located at Östermalm and belongs to the Church of Sweden and is parish church for Hedvig Eleonora Parish in the Diocese of Stockholm.

photo.author: Hedvig_Eleonora_kyrka_December_2012.jpg: Arild Vågen derivative work: ArildV

spots.name: Riddarholmen
spots.summary: Riddarholmen is a small islet in central Stockholm, Sweden. The island forms part of Gamla Stan, the old town, and houses a number of private palaces dating back to the 17th century.

spots.name: ABBA The Museum
spots.summary: ABBA The Museum is a Swedish interactive exhibition about the pop band ABBA that opened in Stockholm, Sweden in May 2013. ABBA's collected works are showcased in a contemporary, interactive setting at Djurgården, Stockholm.

spots.name: House of Nobility

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The House of Nobility in Stockholm, Sweden, is a corporation and a building that maintains records and acts as an interest group on behalf of the Swedish nobility.

spots.name: Tessin Palace

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Tessin Palace is a baroque town house located in Gamla stan, the old town in central Stockholm. Located next to the Royal Palace, it is facing Slottsbacken, the major approach to the Stockholm Palace, and flanked by two alleys, Finska kyrkogränd and Bollhusgränd.

spots.name: Moderna Museet

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: Moderna Museet is a state museum for modern and contemporary art and design, located on the island of Skeppsholmen in central Stockholm, opened in 1958.

photo.author: No machine-readable author provided. Kalle1~commonswiki assumed (based on copyri

spots.name: Hötorget buildings
spots.summary: The Hötorget buildings are five high-rise office buildings in the Stockholm city center in Sweden. Located between the squares Hötorget and Sergels Torg in the central Norrmalm district, they stand 72 m (236 ft) tall and are a clearly visible landmark.

spots.name: Skeppsbron
spots.summary: Skeppsbron is both a street and a quay in Gamla stan, the old town of Stockholm, capital of Sweden, stretching from the bridge Strömbron in front of the Royal Palace southward to Slussen.

spots.name: Old Stockholm telephone tower

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Old Stockholm telephone tower was a metallic structure built to connect approximately 5,500 telephone lines in the Swedish capital of Stockholm. Constructed in 1887, the tower was used until 1913. It was damaged by a fire in 1952 and demolished the following year.

photo.author: Unknown photographer, original kept in the National Museum of Science and Techno

spots.name: Kaknästornet
spots.summary: The Kaknäs tower is a telecommunications tower located at Ladugårdsgärdet in Stockholm, Sweden. The tower is a major hub of Swedish television, radio and satellite broadcasts.

spots.name: Centralbron
spots.summary: Centralbron is a major bridge in central Stockholm, Sweden, connecting the northern district Norrmalm to the southern Södermalm.

spots.name: Skeppsholmen
spots.summary: Skeppsholmen is one of the islands of Stockholm. It is connected with Blasieholmen and Kastellholmen by bridges. It is accessible by foot from Kungsträdgården, past the Grand Hôtel and Nationalmuseum, by bus number 65, or by boat from Slussen, Djurgården or Nybroplan.

spots.name: Stockholm Synagogue

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Great Synagogue of Stockholm is a Conservative Jewish congregation and synagogue, located at 3A Wahrendorffsgatan, close to the park Kungsträdgården on Norrmalm, in Stockholm, Sweden. The synagogue was designed by Fredrik Wilhelm Scholander in the Moorish Revival style and completed in 1870.

spots.name: Mårten Trotzigs Gränd
spots.summary: Mårten Trotzigs gränd is an alley in Gamla stan, the old town of Stockholm, Sweden. Leading from Västerlånggatan and Järntorget up to Prästgatan and Tyska Stallplan, the width of its 37 steps tapers down to a mere 90 centimetres (35 in), making the alley the narrowest street in Stockholm.

spots.name: Engelbrekt Church

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Engelbrekt Church is a protected church located in the Lärkstaden area of Stockholm, Sweden. It belongs to the Evangelical-Lutheran Church of Sweden and is a parish church for Engelbrekt Parish in the Diocese of Stockholm.

spots.name: Saint James's Church

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Saint James's Church is a church in central Stockholm, Sweden, dedicated to apostle Saint James the Greater, patron saint of travellers. It is often mistakenly called St Jacob's. The confusion arises because Swedish, like many other languages, uses the same name for both James and Jacob.

spots.name: Norrbro
spots.summary: Norrbro is an arch bridge over Norrström in central Stockholm, Sweden. It extends north from the northern front of the Royal Palace passing over Helgeandsholmen in front of the Riksdag building, and from there over to Gustav Adolfs torg.

spots.name: Stockholm Court House
spots.summary: The Stockholm Court House is situated on Kungsholmen in Central Stockholm, Sweden. The building is connected to the Stockholm Police House through an underground pedestrian walkway. The Stockholm City Court was situated in the building from 1915 to 1971 and Stockholm District Court from 1971.

spots.name: Haga Palace

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Haga Palace, formerly known as the Queen's Pavilion, is located in Haga Park, Solna Municipality, in Metropolitan Stockholm, Sweden. The palace is today the residence of Victoria, Crown Princess of Sweden, Prince Daniel, Duke of Västergötland, and their family.

spots.name: Katarina Church
spots.summary: Katarina kyrka is a church in central Stockholm, Sweden. The original building was constructed 1656–1695. It has been rebuilt twice after being destroyed by fires, the second time in the 1990s. The Katarina-Sofia borough is named after Katarina Parish and the neighbouring parish of Sofia.

spots.name: Kungsgatan
spots.summary: Kungsgatan is a street in central Stockholm, Sweden. It was formerly a red-light district and is currently a busy shopping street.

spots.name: Mynttorget
spots.summary: Mynttorget is a public square in Gamla stan, the old town in central Stockholm, Sweden.

spots.name: Wrangel Palace

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Wrangel Palace is a townhouse mansion on Riddarholmen islet in Gamla Stan, the old town of Stockholm, Sweden.

spots.name: Liljevalchs konsthall
spots.summary: Liljevalchs konsthall is a kunsthalle art venue located on Djurgården island in Stockholm, Sweden. Designed by architect Carl Bergsten (1879–1935) and inaugurated in March 1916, it is today owned by the City of Stockholm.

spots.name: Bonde Palace

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Bonde Palace is a palace in Gamla stan, the old town in central Stockholm, Sweden.

spots.name: Royal Chapel
spots.summary: The Royal Chapel is a church inside Stockholm Palace. It was opened in 1754. It is the church of the non-territorial parish of the Royal Court, which consist of the Swedish royal family, present and former permanent employees at the Royal Court, and spouse and children of permanent employees.

spots.name: Swedish Museum of Natural History

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: The Swedish Museum of Natural History, in Stockholm, is one of two major museums of natural history in Sweden, the other one being located in Gothenburg.

spots.name: Swedish Army Museum

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: The Swedish Army Museum is a museum of military history located in the district of Östermalm in Stockholm. It reopened in 2002 after a long period of closure, and was awarded the title of the best museum of Stockholm in 2005.

spots.name: Bergianska trädgården
spots.summary: The Bergianska trädgården, the Bergian Garden or Hortus Bergianus, is a botanical garden located in the Frescati area on the outskirts of Stockholm, close to the Swedish Museum of Natural History and the main campus of Stockholm University. The director of the garden is known as Professor Bergianus.

spots.name: Berns salonger
spots.summary: Berns Salonger is a restaurant and entertainment venue, in Berzelii Park, in central Stockholm, Sweden. The building was constructed from 1862 to 1863 by the architect Johan Fredrik Åbom for pastry chef Heinrich Robert Berns and extended in 1886. Berns often holds concerts and other shows and has a capacity of 1,200.

spots.name: Stockholm Concert Hall
spots.summary: The Stockholm Concert Hall is the main hall for orchestral music in Stockholm, Sweden.

spots.name: Stockholm City Hall
spots.summary: The city hall, where the Nobel Prize Banquet takes place every year, is an imposing brick building in the city centre. Guided tours are held daily, and allow you to see the impressive halls used for the Nobel festivities, the Blue Hall and the Golden Hall. The tower offers a great view of the Old Town and can be climbed (optionally, a lift can take you half the way).

spots.name: Swedish Parliament
spots.summary: Free-entrance guided tours in Swedish and English.

spots.name: Galleri Cobra

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Art gallery.

spots.name: Royal Dramatic Theatre
spots.summary: Sweden's national stage for spoken-word drama. The building is impressive in its own right. Guided tours in English.

spots.name: Raoul Wallenberg Monument

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: A monument near the Stockholm Synagogue commemorates Raoul Wallenberg, a diplomat who had 10,000 Jews in Budapest rescued from [[Holocaust remembrance

spots.name: Skansen-Akvariet

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Displays tropical animals such as lemurs, monkeys, snakes, spiders, fish and Cuban crocodiles. The aquarium requires an extra cover charge.

spots.name: Royal Swedish Academy of Fine Arts

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Free entrance. Holds several works from Nationalmuseum. At the same address you can find [http://www.gallerimagnuskarlsson.com/ Galleri Magnus Karlsson] (M-F 12:00-17:00, Sa Su 12:00-16:00), a small, local gallery showcasing local artworks.

spots.name: The Royal Mews
spots.summary: Guided tours and group visits only.

spots.name: blås & knåda

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Ceramics and glassware gallery.

spots.name: Galleri Magnus Karlsson

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: A small, local gallery showcasing local artworks.

spots.name: The Viking Museum

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: A Viking museum opened in 2017. The main attraction is Ragnfrids saga, an 11-minute ride through dioramas depicting a Viking adventure. The ride is a bit scary; children should be at least 7 years old, and accompanied by an adult. There is also an exhibition with replicas of Viking objects. Good for visitors who want a short introduction to the Vikings and are not bothered by the cover charge or t

spots.name: Café Opera and Operakällaren

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: In the building of the Royal Opera, Café Opera has for long been the place if you want to be seen with celebrities. Offers good food and drinks. Dress code applies, entrance fee 220 kr. In the same building you'll find a beautiful dining room of the formal and extremely expensive Operakällaren. If you want a less costly option, consider the other two restaurants at the Opera: Operabaren and Backfi

spots.name: Chokladkoppen & Kaffekoppen
spots.summary: Kaffekoppen and Chokladkoppen (literally, the Coffee Cup and the Chocolate Cup) are two LGBT-friendly sister cafes situated on the Stortorget in Gamla stan, just off the touristy Västerlånggatan. If one is full you can just walk over to the other one. The interior in both of them is small but cosy, probably not for the claustrophobic! Gigantic sandwiches if you're hungry, and if you're looking for

spots.name: Gondolen

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: A fancy and expensive restaurant run by the famous chef Erik Lallerstedt, in the peculiar 1930s elevator building Katarinahissen. There is an inexpensive branch named Köket in the same premises where you can eat the best of Swedish cuisine for considerably less than in the main dining room, although you'll miss out on the fabulous view of the city. Dress code may apply! Mains in main dining room 1

spots.name: Himlen

hours.note: Closed Sun

spots.summary: Once upon a time, the landmark skyscraper on Götgatan housed the offices of the Swedish Tax Agency. After major renovations, the building reopened in 2008, transformed into the unlikely combination of a small shopping mall, student apartments and, on the 25th and 26th floors, an exclusive-looking sky bar and restaurant offering visitors one of the most spectacular panoramas over the city. Enter fr

spots.name: Zocalo

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: A chain of Mexican fast-food restaurants. The restaurants are spacious and have a trendy decor. The service is based on automatic signal devices (no table service) and is very fast - getting your order ready usually takes about five minutes from when you walk in. Try the burritos, that's what the chain is known for. Five restaurants in Stockholm and four elsewhere in Sweden.

spots.name: Leijontornet
spots.summary: Leijontornet is a classical fine diner, and the main restaurant in this local chain. With the foundations of a city wall tower behind glass in the cellar dining room, Leijontornet is about exclusive food with a traditionalist slant in an exclusive historical environment. The street-level bar next door is a surprisingly vivid place with cheaper dishes from the kitchen.

spots.name: Mosebacke Etablissement

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: In the same building as the Södra Teatern theatre and bar, this is a laid-back restaurant, bar and music venue. In the summer, its large beer garden with a panoramic view is extremely popular with Stockholmers and tourists alike. Indoors, you will find lots of clubs and live music in a wealth of genres, including brunches with live jazz on weekends 10:30-03:00.

spots.name: Berns Bar

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Berns Bar is one of the trendier hangouts in the city centre, with a nice lounge and several dancefloors. You can eat a late dinner here to avoid the high entrance fee. Otherwise, make sure to show up early (before 23:00) in order to get in with minimal hassle. 300 kr entrance and mixed drinks costing as much as 150 kr. Can be overcrowded late at night.

spots.name: Sturehof

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Close to Riche, with the same owners and much the same well-to-do clientele, Sturehof's location right on Stureplan draws a slightly more mixed and relaxed crowd than many of its neighbours. The restaurant has good quality food, albeit on the expensive side. The music bar O-baren is well known for its DJ sets.

spots.name: Claes på hörnet

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Tracing its history back to 1731, the inn Claes på Hörnet (in literal translation "Claes on the Corner") serves traditional Swedish food in more or less modern forms. The 18th century-inspired dining environment adds to the enjoyment. The inn also has 10 hotel rooms in 18th century style. Mains 145-265 kr.

spots.name: Ho's

hours.note: Closed Mon, Tue, Wed, Thu

spots.summary: While Stockholm has a fair number of cheap Chinese restaurants, most serve a rather bland and watered-down version of the most popular "westernized" staple dishes. While the competition is not all that fierce, Ho's stand out as a quality choice, with a wide selection of dishes with more spice and taste.

spots.name: Örtagården
spots.summary: On the top floor of the Östermalmshallen food market, Örtagården serves a sumptuous vegetarian buffet with hot and cold vegetarian dishes at a decent price. There is also a "back pocket" serving meat dishes. Vegetarian weekday buffet lunch 85 kr, vegetarian weekday dinner and weekend buffet 135 kr.

spots.name: Sjögräs bar

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Next door to a decent, if a bit expensive, restaurant by the name 'Sjögräs' (Seaweed), specialising in Caribbean fare, this small bar offers a wide selection of rum brands. The standard European beers are still the most popular choices for the young and rather trendy clientele, however.

spots.name: Zum Franziskaner

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: A beer hall which traces its history from the Hanseatic period, the name has allegedly been around since 1471. It has been at its current location since 1906 and most furniture are original. The food is classic Swedish cuisine. Also try also Bakfickan which serves beer and light meals.

spots.name: Hermans

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Sumptuous weekend vegetarian buffet (theme changes weekly) followed by delicious coffees, teas, and desserts (140-190 kr depending on beverage/dessert choice). The view over Stockholm is amazing, go there at sunset and sit on the back terrace. They sometimes have live entertainment.

spots.name: Kvarnen

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: A beer hall with old traditions. Popular with fans of the football club Hammarby IF. This place has expanded, adding more modern, trendy bars in adjoining rooms. Has a wide selection of beers and food at decent prices. Some scenes of the Millennium series were shot here.

spots.name: Peppar

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Awesome Cajun and Creole food at decent prices. Some have argued that they make the best burger in the city. The place is especially known for having excessive decorations at all major holidays like Christmas and Halloween. They also make really good jalapeño bread.

spots.name: Nooshi
spots.summary: An Asian restaurant at the centre of Stockholm, on the ground floor of the culture house Kulturhuset. The location is easily found in central Stockholm. Serves a mixture of cuisine from various Asian countries, including Japan, Korea and Thailand. 100 kr-140 kr.

spots.name: Pelikan

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: An old style working-class beer hall with a very authentic feeling, for those traditionalists who think Kvarnen has sold out. High noise level but quite a friendly crowd. Also offers simple and authentic Swedish food at a reasonable price.

spots.name: Radisson Skybar

hours.note: Closed Sun

spots.summary: Not the most elevated sky bar in the world, in any sense of the word, but if you want a panoramic view to go with your drink this is the only option in the Norrmalm area (although Gondolen's Bar on Södermalm probably has better drinks).
